class.name: Barbarian (legacy)
class.description:
> _Rage consumes you in battle. You delight in wreaking havoc and using powerful weapons to carve through your enemies, relying on astonishing durability without needing complicated techniques or rigid training. Your rages draw upon a vicious instinct, which you might associate with an animal, a spirit, or some part of yourself. To many barbarians, brute force is a hammer and every problem looks like a nail, whereas others try to hold back the storm of emotions inside them and release their rage only when it matters most._

* * *

### **During Combat Encounters…**

You summon your rage and rush to the front lines to smash your way through. Offense is your best defense—you'll need to drop foes before they can exploit your relatively low defenses.

### **During Social Encounters…**

You use intimidation to get what you need, especially when gentler persuasion can't get the job done.

### **While Exploring…**

You look out for danger, ready to rush headfirst into battle in an instant. You climb the challenging rock wall and drop a rope for others to follow, and you wade into the risky currents to reach the hidden switch beneath the water's surface. If something needs breaking, you're up to the task!

### **In Downtime…**

You might head to a tavern to carouse, build up the fearsome legend of your mighty deeds, or recruit followers to become a warlord in your own right.

### **You Might…**

*   Have a deep-seated well of anger, hatred, or frustration.
    
*   Prefer a straightforward approach to one requiring patience and tedium.
    
*   Engage in a regimen of intense physical fitness—and punch anyone who says this conflicts with your distaste for patience and tedium.
    

### **Others Probably…**

*   Rely on your courage and your strength, and trust that you can hold your own in a fight.
    
*   See you as uncivilized or a boorish lout unfit for high society.
    
*   Believe that you are loyal to your friends and allies and will never relent until the fight is done.

background.name: Dauntless
background.description:
> As a child, you chose to face each of your deepest fears and, time and again, emerged victorious. You have learned to conquer fear itself, and by sheer force of will and determination, you're able to brush off frightening experiences more easily than most. Others find it difficult to intimidate you into backing down from whatever you've set your mind to.

Choose two ability boosts. One must be to Wisdom or Charisma, and one is a free ability boost.

You are trained in the [Diplomacy](https://2e.aonprd.com/Skills.aspx?ID=6) skill. You gain the [Indomitable Act](link_feat_29795) reaction.

ancestry.name: Anadi
ancestry.description:
> _Anadi people are reclusive, sapient spiders who hail from the jungles of southern Garund. Though they act in many ways like natural-born shapeshifters, their twin forms actually stem from carefully developed magic._

As a communal and peaceful people, anadi ancestors endeavored to establish trade with the neighbors of their homeland. However, these anadi soon learned that most others found their appearance to be extremely objectionable. Wishing to avoid conflict, ancient anadi retreated into isolation until they could find a solution. The answer came when their greatest scholars innovated a fusion of transmutation and illusion magic that allowed them to assume a [humanoid](link_trait_2399) form. The technique was developed, perfected, and eventually taught to the overwhelming majority of anadi.

Early efforts with their new approach to diplomacy have yielded much better results, though sporadic contact means that some outsiders whisper false legends about anadi, such as claims that they are humans who transform into monstrous spiders at moonrise. Even contemporary explorers have reported anadi as human-spider hybrids. The anadi people of the current day strive to slowly but surely create a world where they no longer need to hide their true nature.

conditions.name: Wounded
conditions.description:
You have been seriously injured. If you lose the dying condition and do not already have the wounded condition, you become wounded 1. If you already have the wounded condition when you lose the dying condition, your wounded condition value increases by 1. If you gain the dying condition while wounded, increase your dying condition value by your wounded value.
    The wounded condition ends if someone successfully restores Hit Points to you using Treat Wounds, or if you are restored to full Hit Points by any means and rest for 10 minutes.

generalAndSkillFeats.name: Crystal Healing
generalAndSkillFeats.description:
You know how to stimulate a body's natural healing abilities through the application of resonant crystals. Doing so requires you to use at least two semiprecious stones with a total value of 5 gp or more in place of healer's tools, which allows you to attempt to [Treat Disease](link_action_19862) or [Treat Poison](link_action_19863) using Occultism rather than Medicine.

If you're an expert in Occultism and you use gems whose total value equals or exceeds 50 gp, you gain a +1 item bonus to your Occultism check. If you're a master and the gems' value equals or exceeds 700 gp, the item bonus increases to +2; if you're legendary in Occultism and the gems' value equals or exceeds 15,000 gp, the item bonus increases to +3.

generalAndSkillFeats.name: Ride
generalAndSkillFeats.description: When you Command an Animal you're mounted on to take a move action (such as [Stride](link_action_19855)), you automatically succeed instead of needing to attempt a check. Any animal you're mounted on acts on your turn, like a minion. If you Mount an animal in the middle of an encounter, it skips its next turn and then acts on your next turn.

generalAndSkillFeats.name: Sparkling Performance
generalAndSkillFeats.description: Your presence lights up the stage. You can [Create a Diversion](link_action_19619) using Performance instead of Deception. If you’re a master in Performance, you can create sparkles when you attempt a Performance check, casting dim light in a 20-foot radius. If you’re legendary in Performance, you can cast bright light in a 20-foot radius and attempt to [counteract](link_action_27519) a [darkness](link_trait_1900) effect using your Performance modifier as your [counteract](link_action_27519) modifier.

generalAndSkillFeats.name: Specialty Crafting
generalAndSkillFeats.description: Your training focused on Crafting one particular kind of item. Select one of the specialties listed below; you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Crafting checks to [Craft](link_action_19617) items of that type. If you are a master in Crafting, this bonus increases to +2. If it's unclear whether the specialty applies, the GM decides. Some specialties might apply only partially. For example, if you were making a [morningstar](link_item_7598) and had specialty in woodworking, the GM might give you half your bonus because the item requires both blacksmithing and woodworking.

classFeats.name: Draconic Arrogance
classFeats.description: Few can sway you from your goals while the fury of combat fills you. While [raging](link_feat_31184), you gain a +2 status bonus to saving throws against [emotion](link_trait_1486) effects.

classFeats.name: Quick-Tempered
classFeats.requirements: You are not encumbered or wearing heavy armor.
classFeats.description: So long as you are able to move freely, your fury is instinctive and instantaneous. You [Rage](link_feat_31184).

classFeats.name: Rage
classFeats.description:
You tap into your inner fury and begin raging. You gain a number of temporary Hit Points equal to your level plus your Constitution modifier (⬆️{{level+attribute\_con}}). While you are raging:

*   You deal 2 additional damage on melee [Strikes](link_action_19856). This additional damage is halved if your weapon or [unarmed](link_trait_2398) attack is [agile](link_trait_1569).
    
*   You can’t use actions with the [concentrate](link_trait_1432) trait unless they also have the [rage](link_trait_1455) trait. You can [Seek](link_action_19845) while raging.
    

Rage lasts for 1 minute, until you fall unconscious, or until the encounter ends, whichever comes first. You can’t voluntarily stop raging. When you stop raging, you lose any remaining temporary Hit Points from Rage, and can’t gain temporary Hit Points from using the Rage action again for 1 minute.

classFeats.name: Sudden Charge
classFeats.description: With a quick sprint, you dash up to your foe and swing. [Stride](link_action_19855) twice. If you end your movement within melee reach of at least one enemy, you can make a melee [Strike](link_action_19856) against that enemy. You can use Sudden Charge while [Burrowing](link_action_19609), [Climbing](link_action_19612), [Flying](link_action_19721), or [Swimming](link_action_19859) instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

classFeats.name: Intimidating Strike
classFeats.description: Your blow not only wounds creatures but also shatters their confidence. Make a melee [Strike](link_action_19856). If you hit and deal damage, the target is frightened 1, or frightened 2 on a critical hit.

classFeats.name: Second Wind
classFeats.description: You can enter a second rage, but afterward you need to catch your breath. When you [Rage](link_feat_31184), you can choose to gain temporary HP from the [Rage](link_feat_31184) even if 1 minute hasn’t passed (or a full turn if you have the [revitalizing rage](link_class-feature_31241) class feature). If you do, once this [Rage](link_feat_31184) ends you become fatigued until you rest for 10 minutes.

ancestryFeats.name: Web Walker
ancestryFeats.description: You have plenty of practice navigating webs. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saves and AC against the [_web_](link_spell_6196) spell, natural webbing, and effects that entrap you in webbing, as well as a +1 circumstance bonus against other effects that snare and entangle you, like the [_entangling flora_](link_spell_4602) spell. Whenever you roll a success on a saving throw against an effect involving a web, you get a critical success instead.

ancestryFeats.name: Web Weaver
ancestryFeats.description: You can produce a soft silk to weave into useful items. You gain the [Specialty Crafting](link_feat_20570) feat with a specialty in weaving. You can use your webbing to [Craft](link_action_19617) simple, nonconsumable threaded items, such as clothing and rope, at zero cost as long as their base Price is 1 sp or less. These items have no resale value, and they naturally degrade after 24 hours without regular (if minor) maintenance. You can maintain up to 10 such items at a time; if you create a new one, your oldest creation breaks down from neglect. These temporary items take you only 1 day to [Craft](link_action_19617) instead of 4. If you're an expert in Crafting, you can [Craft](link_action_19617) these items in 1 hour; if you're a master, you can [Craft](link_action_19617) them in 10 minutes; if you're legendary, you can [Craft](link_action_19617) them in 1 minute.

otherFeats.name: Spirit Instinct
otherFeats.description:
Whether you are emotionally sensitive to the spirits around you; worship ancestors or apparitions; or are haunted by the specter of an ancestor, relative, friend, or foe, your rage takes the form of a spiritual possession.

**Instinct Ability—Spirit Rage** When you [rage](link_feat_31184), you can increase the additional damage from [Rage](link_feat_31184) from 2 to 3 and change its damage type to [spirit](link_trait_1556), instead of the damage type for your weapon or unarmed attack (choose each time you [Rage](link_feat_31184)). If you choose to deal [spirit](link_trait_1556) damage, your weapon or [unarmed](link_trait_2398) attack gains the effects of the [ghost touch](link_item_6992) property rune, which makes it more effective against [incorporeal](link_trait_2424) creatures, and your [Rage](link_feat_31184) action gains the [divine](link_trait_1475) and [spirit](link_trait_1556) traits.

**Specialization Ability (7th)** When using spirit rage, increase the damage from [Rage](link_feat_31184) from 3 to 7. If you have [greater weapon specialization](link_class-feature_31226), instead increase the damage when using spirit rage to 13.

**Raging Resistance (9th)** You resist [void](link_trait_1485) damage, as well as damage dealt by the attacks and abilities of [undead](link_trait_2425) creatures, regardless of the damage type.

physicalFeatures.name: Change Shape
physicalFeatures.description: You change into your human or spider shape. Each shape has a specific, persistent appearance. In your [human](link_trait_1436) shape, you can't use [unarmed](link_trait_2398) attacks granted by your ancestry. You aren't flat-footed when [climbing](link_action_19612) in your spider shape. However, in your spider shape you can't use weapons, shields, or other held items of any sort, and you are limited in what actions you can take that have the [manipulate](link_trait_1433) trait. The only [manipulate](link_trait_1433) actions you can take are to [Cast a Spell](link_action_19611) , weave silk or webbing, or simple [Interact](link_action_19733) actions such as opening an unlocked door. Your spider legs can't perform actions that require fingers or significant manual dexterity, including any action that would require a check to accomplish. The GM might determine other manipulate actions are appropriate for your spider legs.

physicalFeatures.name: Fangs
physicalFeatures.description: You were born with a natural means for hunting and self-defense. You gain a [fangs](link_item_14437) [unarmed](link_trait_2398) attack that deals 1d6 piercing damage. Your [fangs](link_item_14437) are in the brawling group and have the [finesse](link_trait_1570) and [unarmed](link_trait_2398) traits.

data.text: Your [fangs](link_item_14437) attack has the [grapple](link_trait_2524) and [trip](link_trait_1537) traits.

heritages.description: You were hatched with hooked fangs that give you an edge when hunting in your true form. Your [fangs](link_item_14437) attack gains the [grapple](link_trait_2524) and [trip](link_trait_1537) traits.

sense.name: Normal Vision
sense.description:
In bright light, such as sunlight, you can observe things clearly. However, creatures and objects in areas of dim light have the concealed condition for you and, in darkness, they're hidden or undetected.  
  
You have the blinded condition while in darkness, though you may be able to see illuminated areas beyond the darkness. If you can see into an illuminated area, it can observe creatures within that illuminated area normally. After being in darkness, sudden exposure to bright light might make you dazzled for a short time, as determined by the GM.

sense.name: Hearing
sense.description: Hearing is the ability to perceive sound by detecting vibrations through an organ such as the ear. A creature might be undetected by you if it’s in an environment that distorts the sense, such as a noisy room. In those cases, you have to use the [Seek](link_action_19845) basic action to detect the creature.

sense.name: Smell
sense.description: Smell allows you to detect and identify chemical substances in your environment through your [olfactory](link_trait_2131) system. This involves the detection of odor molecules by receptor cells in the nose.
